title: Netflix Data Feedback Loop
summary: How member behavior moves through streaming, durable data products, and personalization systems.

nodes.label: Device events
nodes.description: Playback, search, impression, and interaction events from the product surface.

nodes.label: Keystone + Kafka
nodes.description: The streaming backbone that collects and routes high-volume events.

nodes.label: Flink processors
nodes.description: Stateful and stateless processing turns raw events into useful streams.

nodes.label: Iceberg data products
nodes.description: Durable tables support backfills, analytics, and training workloads.

nodes.label: Model training
nodes.description: Batch and nearline features train personalization and ranking models.

nodes.label: Personalized experience
nodes.description: Rows, search, artwork, and title choices adapt to member behavior.

steps.title: Capture member behavior
steps.description: Every useful recommendation starts as product behavior that can be safely collected and routed.

steps.title: Process streams in parallel
steps.description: Streaming jobs serve freshness-sensitive features while raw and curated events continue toward durable storage.

steps.title: Serve fresh context
steps.description: Near-real-time processors can update product-facing context without waiting for the next full batch cycle.

steps.title: Train from durable history
steps.description: Warehouse and lakehouse tables make longer histories available for model training, audits, and backfills.

steps.title: Close the feedback loop
steps.description: The personalized surface changes what members do next, creating the next round of training and evaluation data.
